1rkx3jn:220: The article's core formula: evaluation set = agent training data. Finding good data + finding a good fitting function = improving the agent. This view unifies all agent improvement methods (SFT/RL, harness engineering, memory libraries) as a "data integration problem"—differing only in where the integration targets: weights, configuration, or context. This unified framework steers teams away from "chasing whatever is hot" toward data-driven decisions: analyze traces → identify improvements → curate evaluation sets → run experiments, forming a measurable, reproducible improvement flywheel.
1snpwx:232: Scaling Dreaming describes the process of integrating agent data back into the agent itself over large-scale data and long time spans. It differs from traditional "scaling laws" in that it focuses not on simple growth in model parameters or training data volume, but on the cyclical process by which interaction data generated by agents in real environments is systematically collected, distilled, and reinjected into the agent system. This is a paradigm shift from "passive training" to "active evolution"—an agent is no longer a static artifact after a single training run, but a system that continuously learns from its own experience.
